pos.personaBrief: Trapattoni's catenaccio-derived zona mista relied on devastating counter-attacks and transition speed over keeping the ball (TFT transitions facts, Wikipedia zona mista), so he never chased possession for its own sake.

pro.personaBrief: Counter-attacking, space-seeking play with a sweeper as springboard (Scirea) and a conservative philosophy favours quick vertical play and safe, simple choices over risky short build-up.

est.personaBrief: A system-over-individuals coach with defined roles (Gentile marker, Scirea libero, Cabrini on the flank) and a rehearsed structure, not fluid relational play.

lar.personaBrief: TFT stresses creating and exploiting space on the wing and the edge of the box, with Cabrini as extra winger and an advanced left flank, though stars played centrally.

blo.personaBrief: Low-to-mid block with counter-attacks, compact back line and 19 goals conceded in the Inter title season; no evidence of pressing high.

mar.personaBrief: Zona mista with man-marking as near-religion (Il Foglio) and Gentile assigned to opposing fantasistas, though he adopted some zonal elements.

pla.personaBrief: Imposed a system on players (system over individuals) while adapting tactically, studying opponents' habits and neutralising stars; kept the plan level at half-time.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic, conservative, result-first maestro of calcio all'italiana; conservative preference over Klinsmann's free-flowing approach.

sis.personaBrief: Philosophy stressed the system over individuals, refused to overload the XI with flair players, benched superstars at Bayern, and everyone does their job.

jog.personaBrief: Valued disciplined, tough, all-action players (Gentile, Matthaus) and the rigours of the Italian game, while still using Platini; limited room for non-runners.

bas.personaBrief: Built title teams with seasoned veterans and stars (Zoff, Matthaus, Brehme, Platini), and preferred a fit experienced fringe player; youth development was not a theme.

lid.personaBrief: Authoritarian: closed training to the press, omitted superstars, publicly berated players ('Ich habe fertig'), and the line-up was his alone.
